description: Multi-source catalogue of placement evidence for metabolic subsystems on overview maps. Evidence is kept per source; inconsistencies between maps are preserved and summarised in 'consensus' rather than resolved.

coordinate_frame.direction_semantics: 'direction' always gives the position of TARGET relative to ANCHOR

relationship_vocabulary.FEEDS: directed: material flows from anchor into target (via lists the connecting metabolites)
relationship_vocabulary.SHARES_HUB: undirected: both use the listed branch-point metabolites; attach at them
relationship_vocabulary.ALTERNATIVE_ROUTE: undirected: alternative routes between shared endpoints; draw in parallel
relationship_vocabulary.REVERSE_OF: undirected: opposing directions of (largely) the same transformations; draw side by side
relationship_vocabulary.COFACTOR_SUPPLY: directed: anchor makes a cofactor the target needs; weak, never pulls layouts together
relationship_vocabulary.ENERGY_COUPLING: directed: anchor supplies ATP/reductant/proton motive force to target
relationship_vocabulary.TRANSPORT: directed: link crosses a compartment boundary; transporter sits on the boundary

strength_definitions.hard: Strong biochemical/structural constraint; preserve unless impossible or context conflicts.
strength_definitions.weak: Do not enforce adjacency; use as a light hint or connector only.

consensus_definitions.agreement_R: length of the weighted mean unit vector over sources (1 = all sources point the same way)
consensus_definitions.suggested_strength: strong: agreement with >=3 sources; medium: agreement with 2; weak: partial or single source; none: conflict
consensus_definitions.levels: exact = as observed; pathway = modules and hubs lifted to their pathway so that sources of different granularity meet

The oxidative and non-oxidative phases form connected submodules; the non-oxidative phase rearranges pentoses into glycolytic intermediates.
Ribose-5-phosphate feeds PRPP synthesis, so PRPP should follow the PPP toward nucleotide metabolism.

The glycerol-3-phosphate shuttle transfers cytosolic reducing equivalents to mitochondrial electron transport.
Triose-phosphate export connects chloroplast carbon fixation to cytosolic sucrose synthesis.

Lipid exchange and specialised lipid pathways connect ER and mitochondria.

cycle_layouts.note: Classic Krebs orientation (Lehninger, Roche chart, KEGG 00020/01100). Many Escher maps unroll the cycle instead; treat as preference.
Fixation - reduction - regeneration; draw adjacent to the PPP so shared sugar phosphates align.
Mitochondrial half (carbamoyl-P, citrulline) on the boundary side; fumarate exit toward TCA.
Draw as a chord across the TCA ring.

role_conventions.statement: biosynthesis pathways left (west), energy metabolism middle, degradation pathways right (east)

policies.statement: Phosphate and polyphosphate pools interact with nucleotide phosphorylation and energy charge.
Substrate-level ATP/GTP-forming steps occur within glycolysis and TCA-linked catabolism.
ATP production supplies biosynthetic work broadly; treat this as a global supporting link, not a reason to pull all anabolic pathways together.
Show cofactor supply links to users selectively; ubiquitous cofactor usage should not dominate global geometry.
Tailoring, export, resistance and product degradation subsystems belong near their parent natural-product pathway.
Draw complex-substrate breakdown from the map periphery toward central carbon/energy hubs.
Draw central precursor pools as branching outward toward biosynthetic families.
Where a clear biochemical precursor-product relationship exists, arrange the producing module upstream of the consuming module.
Product degradation/recycling should be near the product pathway but may extend toward central catabolism.
Keep closely related pathway families contiguous without forcing a fixed compass direction.
Strongly shared carbon-skeleton intermediates justify local proximity; downweight ubiquitous currency compounds.
Place pathways inside the same compartment region when the relevant enzymes are co-localised.
Transporter nodes should lie on the boundary between source and destination regions.
Global ATP coupling should be shown as a link but should not pull all ATP users into one local cluster.
Show cofactor supply/use links, but avoid global clustering based only on ubiquitous cofactors.
Regulatory dependencies should generally be represented as overlays rather than as carbon-flow placement constraints.
Alternative routes for the same substrate/product should be displayed in parallel and rejoin at shared endpoints where possible.
Place branches around a shared metabolite anchor and order them by functional family or product class.
Cycle inputs/outputs should attach at the specific intermediate rather than arbitrarily to the cycle boundary.
ATP, NAD(H), NADP(H), water, phosphate and protons are generally poor proximity signals by themselves.
